The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Former Robinhood engineer pleads guilty to insider trading scheme on Hyperliquid. Huaisong Xiang admitted using confidential crypto listing information to make $125,523 trading perpetual futures on Hyperliquid. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin risks falling below $60,000 as Nvidia earnings threaten to deepen crypto sell-off. Rising bond yields, ETF outflows and forced selling are weighing on bitcoin as traders brace for more losses. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

U.S. Senate Democrats tell CFTC to back off its demand prediction markets defy bans. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission directed platforms such as Kalshi to defy state bans, but the Democrats want it to reverse course, citing court orders. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Lighter suspends all withdrawals after $10.4 million crypto exploit. The decentralized exchange blamed a leaked trading API key and said its smart contracts were unaffected, while investigators traced funds to Hyperliquid. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Brazil's central bank faces backlash over stablecoin money laundering remarks. A central bank official reportedly said legitimate funds become tainted when moved into stablecoins, comparing the market to the informal "dólar-cabo" system. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

German parliament proposes crypto seizures without criminal charges. German lawyers said a proposed law allowing the seizure of assets worth more than 100,000 euros could impose a burden of proof on crypto holders rather than the authorities. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $65,348 with a +0.31% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,828.98 with a +0.21% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.

items.title: Crypto Today: Bitcoin, Ethereum, XRP tick lower amid mixed ETF flows
items.description: Institutional investors staged a comeback on Monday, with $527 million in Bitcoin spot Exchange-Traded Funds (ETFs), up from roughly $82 million in outflows last Friday. Broadly, cumulative inflows stand at $57.4 billion, with net assets under management at $105 billion, according to SoSoValue data. A steady inflow pattern would cushion Bitcoin against headwinds, increasing the odds of a recovery. [...] Ethereum spot ETFs, on the other hand, recorded $103 million in outflows on Monday, sustaining a four-day bearish streak. Looking back, since September 29, ETH ETFs have posted only one day of inflows, totaling $25 million on October 13. [...] Quoc Dat Tong, senior financial market strategist at Exness, says that the latest ETH spot ETFs "do not tell us why every investor sold. Some may be taking profits, while others may be reducing how much money they have in cryptocurrencies. The funds also represent only part of the ether market." "Even so, continued withdrawals suggest that this source of demand remains weaker than it was during the strong buying seen in late September," he adds.

items.title: Ethereum ETFs Outpace Bitcoin ETFs in 2026 Inflows
items.description:
Ethereum ETF inflows into U.S. spot Ethereum (CRYPTO:ETH) funds reached approximately $1.5 billion, surpassing the $985 million that spot Bitcoin (CRYPTO:BTC) ETFs brought in. This data, sourced from SoSoValue, shows daily crypto ETF inflows and outflows. Spot ETFs directly hold the coins, so their share prices rise and fall with the cryptocurrency's market value. [...] Ethereum ETFs pulled in $1.5B in 2026 inflows, topping Bitcoin's $985M, yet Bitcoin ETFs still hold $109B in total assets, a figure roughly six times greater.

items.description:
Cryptocurrency regulation is no longer a theoretical debate—it’s an evolving framework that is beginning to take shape worldwide. In the United States, Congress has moved toward establishing federal oversight of stablecoins and digital asset markets. The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established a federal regulatory framework for stablecoins, while broader market structure legislation known as the CLARITY Act advanced in Congress in 2026 but has yet to become law. [...] The GENIUS Act, signed into law in 2025, established the first federal regulatory framework for stablecoins in the United States. It limits who can issue stablecoins and requires issuers to maintain reserves backing the tokens they have issued, make monthly disclosures detailing the assets held in reserve, and comply with anti–money laundering and consumer protection requirements.
